title: Live Host Discovered
description: A host was confirmed active on the network by responding to one or more probe types (ICMP, TCP SYN, ARP, or UDP), expanding the known attack surface.
remediation: Reconcile all discovered hosts against the authorised asset inventory and investigate any unexpected or unregistered hosts.

title: Open Port Discovered
description: A TCP or UDP port was confirmed open on the target host, indicating an exposed service that contributes to the overall network attack surface.
remediation: Inventory all open ports against expected service requirements; close or restrict access to ports that serve no legitimate business purpose via host-based or network firewall rules.

title: Service Version Identified
description: A specific software version was identified from a service banner or nmap version detection. This information can be cross-referenced against CVE databases to identify known vulnerabilities.
remediation: Suppress version information where possible. Keep all identified services up to date.

title: DHCP Lease Assigned to Device
description: The device successfully obtained a DHCP lease from the gearbox DHCP server. The assigned IP address and MAC address are documented for the assessment.
remediation: No action required; informational record.

title: LLMNR/NBT-NS Broadcast Poisoning Possible
description: LLMNR and/or NBT-NS broadcast name resolution is active on the network, allowing an attacker to poison responses with Responder and capture NTLMv1/v2 hashes for offline cracking or relay.
remediation: Disable LLMNR and NetBIOS-NS via Group Policy (Network > DNS Client) and enforce DNS-only name resolution across all hosts.

title: LLMNR/NBT-NS Broadcast Poisoning Possible
description: LLMNR and/or NBT-NS broadcast name resolution is active on the network, allowing an attacker to poison responses with Responder and capture NTLMv1/v2 hashes for offline cracking or relay.
remediation: Disable LLMNR and NetBIOS-NS via Group Policy (Network > DNS Client) and enforce DNS-only name resolution across all hosts.

title: NTLM Hash Captured via Responder
description: Responder successfully captured an NTLMv1 or NTLMv2 challenge-response hash in response to a poisoned LLMNR/NBT-NS reply. The captured hash can be subjected to offline dictionary or brute-force cracking or used directly in NTLM relay attacks.
remediation: Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS as described in GB-DISC-005/006. Enforce SMB signing. Implement network segmentation. Use strong, unique passwords resistant to offline cracking.

title: Cleartext Credentials in Traffic Capture
description: Cleartext credentials (username/password) were observed in captured network traffic. The device transmitted authentication information over an unencrypted protocol (e.g., HTTP Basic Auth, FTP, Telnet, SNMP v1/v2c).
remediation: Replace all cleartext authentication protocols with encrypted equivalents. Use TLS for web, SSH for remote management, SNMPv3 for SNMP.

title: Weak or Default Credentials Accepted
description: The target accepted well-known default or factory-set credentials, granting unauthorised access.
remediation: Replace all default credentials with strong, unique secrets and enforce a password policy prior to any deployment.

title: Nessus Critical Vulnerability
description: Nessus Professional identified a critical severity vulnerability (CVSS ≥ 9.0). This typically represents unauthenticated remote code execution, authentication bypass with full system impact, or a well-known exploit with active weaponisation.
remediation: Apply vendor patch immediately. If no patch is available, implement network isolation and document as an accepted risk with a defined remediation timeline.

title: Nessus High Vulnerability
description: Nessus Professional identified a high severity vulnerability (CVSS 7.0–8.9). Often exploitable by local or adjacent attackers with limited prerequisites.
remediation: Patch within the defined SLA for high-severity findings. Apply compensating controls if immediate patching is not feasible.

title: Nessus Medium Vulnerability
description: Nessus Professional identified a medium severity vulnerability (CVSS 4.0–6.9). May require special conditions to exploit but presents meaningful risk.
remediation: Schedule remediation within the standard patch cycle.

title: Nessus Low / Informational Finding
description: Nessus Professional identified a low-severity or informational finding. May represent configuration observations or version disclosures without direct exploitability.
remediation: Include in routine hardening backlog.

title: CVE-Matched Service Banner
description: The service banner matched a known CVE in the NVD or OSV.dev database. The software version identified in the banner is listed as affected by a publicly disclosed vulnerability with an available CVSS score.
remediation: Update the affected software to a patched version. Cross-reference the specific CVE for vendor-recommended mitigations.

title: End-of-Life Software Detected
description: A service banner or version string indicates software that has passed its vendor end-of-life date. No further security patches will be issued, and any future vulnerabilities will be permanently unaddressed.
remediation: Upgrade to a supported version. If upgrade is constrained, apply network isolation and create a formal remediation plan.

title: End-of-Life Operating System Detected
description: The operating system identified from banners or Nessus output has passed its vendor support end-of-life date. The OS will not receive security patches for newly discovered vulnerabilities.
remediation: Upgrade to a supported OS version. If the device cannot be upgraded, implement network isolation as a compensating control.

title: Nuclei Template Match — CVE
description: Nuclei matched a CVE-tagged template against the target. The response pattern confirms the service is exhibiting behaviour consistent with the disclosed vulnerability.
remediation: Apply the vendor patch for the matched CVE. Verify remediation by re-running the nuclei scan.

title: Nuclei Template Match — Misconfiguration
description: Nuclei identified a security misconfiguration (exposed admin panel, default path, misconfigured CORS, insecure HTTP method, etc.).
remediation: Correct the specific misconfiguration. Harden the service configuration against the ProjectDiscovery misconfiguration template library.

title: Nuclei Template Match — Exposed Panel
description: Nuclei identified an exposed administrative or management panel accessible without prior authentication (e.g., Grafana, Jenkins, Kibana, phpMyAdmin, device management UI).
remediation: Restrict access to administrative panels by IP allowlist, VPN, or disable public access entirely.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Expired
description: The server's TLS certificate has passed its expiry date, causing browser trust errors and indicating a breakdown in certificate lifecycle management.
remediation: Renew the certificate immediately and implement automated renewal (e.g., ACME/Let's Encrypt) to prevent future expiry.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Self-Signed
description: The server presented a self-signed TLS certificate that is not anchored to a publicly trusted CA, preventing clients from verifying the server's identity and enabling trivial MITM attacks.
remediation: Replace self-signed certificates with certificates issued by a trusted CA; use ACME/Let's Encrypt for cost-free automation.

title: SSL/TLS — Protocol Version Below TLS 1.2
description: TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 is accepted. These protocol versions are deprecated by RFC 8996 and vulnerable to BEAST, POODLE, and RC4 downgrade attacks.
remediation: Disable TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, and all SSL versions. Accept only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

title: SSL/TLS — Weak Cipher Suite Accepted
description: The TLS server accepts cipher suites providing less than 128-bit security, null encryption, or anonymous key exchange.
remediation: Configure the server to accept only AEAD cipher suites with forward secrecy (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, etc.).

title: SSL/TLS — CRIME / BEAST / LUCKY13 Vulnerability
description: The TLS configuration is susceptible to a compression-based oracle (CRIME), cipher-block chaining attack (BEAST), or timing side-channel (LUCKY13). Specific vulnerability depends on testssl.sh output.
remediation: Disable TLS compression. Migrate to TLS 1.2+ with AES-GCM-only cipher suites. Apply server-side BEAST mitigation (RC4 disabled, prefer AES-GCM).

title: SSL/TLS — Missing HSTS Header
description: The HTTPS service does not return a Strict-Transport-Security header. Clients may be susceptible to SSL stripping attacks.
remediation: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload to all HTTPS responses.

title: SSL/TLS — Weak Certificate Signature Algorithm
description: The TLS certificate is signed with a deprecated algorithm such as MD5 or SHA-1. These algorithms are vulnerable to collision attacks that could allow certificate forgery.
remediation: Reissue the certificate using SHA-256 or SHA-384 as the signature algorithm.

title: SSL/TLS — Certificate Hostname Mismatch
description: The Common Name or Subject Alternative Names in the TLS certificate do not match the host being connected to. Clients will receive a certificate warning or reject the connection.
remediation: Reissue the certificate with the correct Subject Alternative Names matching all DNS names and IP addresses used to access the service.

title: SSH Weak Configuration (Ciphers / Legacy Protocol / Credential Auth)
description: The SSH service is configured with one or more weaknesses including weak ciphers/MACs, SSHv1 support, permitted root login, or password-based authentication, increasing exposure to brute-force and protocol-level attacks.
remediation: Harden sshd_config to disable SSHv1, restrict ciphers and MACs to strong algorithms, disable root login, disable password authentication, and require public-key authentication only.

title: SSH Weak Configuration (Ciphers / Legacy Protocol / Credential Auth)
description: The SSH service is configured with one or more weaknesses including weak ciphers/MACs, SSHv1 support, permitted root login, or password-based authentication, increasing exposure to brute-force and protocol-level attacks.
remediation: Harden sshd_config to disable SSHv1, restrict ciphers and MACs to strong algorithms, disable root login, disable password authentication, and require public-key authentication only.

title: SSH Weak Configuration (Ciphers / Legacy Protocol / Credential Auth)
description: The SSH service is configured with one or more weaknesses including weak ciphers/MACs, SSHv1 support, permitted root login, or password-based authentication, increasing exposure to brute-force and protocol-level attacks.
remediation: Harden sshd_config to disable SSHv1, restrict ciphers and MACs to strong algorithms, disable root login, disable password authentication, and require public-key authentication only.

title: SSH Weak Configuration (Ciphers / Legacy Protocol / Credential Auth)
description: The SSH service is configured with one or more weaknesses including weak ciphers/MACs, SSHv1 support, permitted root login, or password-based authentication, increasing exposure to brute-force and protocol-level attacks.
remediation: Harden sshd_config to disable SSHv1, restrict ciphers and MACs to strong algorithms, disable root login, disable password authentication, and require public-key authentication only.

title: SSH Weak Configuration (Ciphers / Legacy Protocol / Credential Auth)
description: The SSH service is configured with one or more weaknesses including weak ciphers/MACs, SSHv1 support, permitted root login, or password-based authentication, increasing exposure to brute-force and protocol-level attacks.
remediation: Harden sshd_config to disable SSHv1, restrict ciphers and MACs to strong algorithms, disable root login, disable password authentication, and require public-key authentication only.

title: SMB Signing Disabled or Not Required
description: SMB packet signing is not enforced on the server, allowing an attacker positioned between client and server to relay or tamper with SMB authentication and data.
remediation: Enable and require SMB signing via Group Policy (RequireSecuritySignature=1) on all Windows systems to prevent NTLM relay attacks.

title: SMB Share Accessible Without Authentication
description: One or more SMB shares are accessible without valid credentials, allowing unauthenticated users to read or write files and potentially enumerate domain information.
remediation: Require authentication on all SMB shares, disable null-session and guest access, and enforce least-privilege ACLs on every share.

title: SMB Share Accessible Without Authentication
description: One or more SMB shares are accessible without valid credentials, allowing unauthenticated users to read or write files and potentially enumerate domain information.
remediation: Require authentication on all SMB shares, disable null-session and guest access, and enforce least-privilege ACLs on every share.

title: Web — Default Credentials Accepted
description: The web management interface accepted default manufacturer credentials. An attacker can gain full administrative access without any reconnaissance.
remediation: Enforce mandatory credential change on first boot or provisioning. Implement account lockout after failed attempts.

title: Directory Listing Enabled
description: The web server is configured to display a browsable directory index, exposing file structure and potentially sensitive files to unauthenticated users.
remediation: Disable directory indexing (e.g., Options -Indexes in Apache; autoindex off in nginx) and ensure every directory contains an explicit index document.

title: Web — Missing Security Headers
description: One or more recommended HTTP security headers are absent: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.
remediation: Add all recommended security headers to HTTP responses. Review shcheck output for the specific missing headers.

title: Header Data Leakage: Server
description: The HTTP Server response header reveals the web server software name and version, reducing the attacker's reconnaissance effort needed to identify version-specific vulnerabilities.
remediation: Remove or genericise the Server response header in the web server configuration (e.g., ServerTokens Prod in Apache; server_tokens off in nginx).

title: Web — HTTP Exposed (No HTTPS Redirect)
description: The web application is accessible over plaintext HTTP and does not redirect to HTTPS. Credentials and session tokens transmitted over HTTP are observable to network attackers.
remediation: Redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS. Enable HSTS to prevent downgrade attacks.

title: Web — Insecure Cookie Attributes
description: Session or authentication cookies are missing the Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes. This exposes them to theft via JavaScript, plaintext transmission, or CSRF.
remediation: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Strict (or Lax) attributes on all authentication and session cookies.

title: Unencrypted Service: Telnet
description: A Telnet service is accessible on the network, transmitting all data including authentication credentials in cleartext, enabling passive interception or active MITM attacks.
remediation: Disable the Telnet daemon and replace it with SSH for all remote administration; block port 23 at the network perimeter.

title: SNMP Default Community String Accepted
description: The SNMP service accepts a well-known default community string (e.g., public/private), allowing unauthenticated read (and potentially write) access to device configuration data.
remediation: Change all SNMP community strings to random high-entropy values, restrict SNMP access by source IP, and migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption.

title: FTP Anonymous Login Permitted
description: The FTP service accepts the anonymous username without credentials, potentially exposing hosted files or allowing unauthenticated file upload.
remediation: Disable anonymous FTP in the server configuration; migrate file transfer to SFTP/FTPS and enforce authentication for all access.

title: NFS World-Readable Export
description: An NFS export is accessible to all hosts (wildcard * or 0.0.0.0/0 in /etc/exports). Any host on the network can mount and read the exported filesystem.
remediation: Restrict NFS exports by client IP. Use root_squash and nosuid mount options. Disable NFS if not required.

title: Deprecated or Weak Protocol in Use
description: A deprecated or inherently weak network protocol was identified (e.g., RPC portmapper, rsh, rlogin, finger, X11 without auth, TFTP). These protocols provide no confidentiality or authentication.
remediation: Disable deprecated protocol services. Replace with modern, authenticated, encrypted equivalents.

title: mDNS / Bonjour Service Announcement
description: The device is broadcasting mDNS (Multicast DNS / Bonjour / Avahi) service announcements. These expose device capabilities, hostname, model information, and available services to all hosts on the local segment.
remediation: Disable mDNS service announcement on production devices if not required for operation. Apply network segmentation to prevent mDNS traffic crossing boundaries.

title: RFID Card UID Captured
description: Proxmark3 successfully read the UID of an RFID credential within range of the device reader. Systems relying solely on UID for access control are vulnerable to cloning attacks.
remediation: Implement mutual authentication (MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3 with AES). Do not rely on UID alone.

title: RFID Card Data Payload Read
description: The RFID card data blocks were successfully read without authentication. Sensitive data stored in card memory (employee ID, access level, personal data) may be exposed.
remediation: Enable sector access conditions on MIFARE Classic cards. Migrate to DESFire with application-level encryption.

title: RFID Replay Attack Successful
description: A captured RFID credential was successfully replayed to the reader and accepted. No anti-replay protection is in place.
remediation: Replace credential infrastructure with challenge-response or rolling code systems. Audit physical access logs for anomalous events.

title: USB HID Keyboard Injection Accepted
description: The device accepted keystroke injection from an emulated HID keyboard without any restriction or rate-limiting. A pre-programmed HID device can execute OS-level commands on device insertion.
remediation: Implement USB HID device allowlisting. Disable USB HID enumeration on production devices where not required.

title: USB Bash Bunny Payload Executed
description: A Bash Bunny HID payload was executed by the device. The injected keystrokes were processed without restriction.
remediation: Apply USB device policy and application whitelisting. Review autorun and HID handling in the OS.

title: USB Abnormal Power Draw
description: Abnormal USB power characteristics were detected, potentially indicating a rogue charging cable or peripheral with embedded circuitry.
remediation: Deploy USB power-only data-blockers on charging ports. Restrict USB host mode to known-good peripherals.

title: HDMI CEC Command Injection Accepted
description: Injected HDMI CEC commands were accepted and processed. An attacker with HDMI port access can issue remote control commands or exploit CEC stack vulnerabilities.
remediation: Disable CEC in firmware if not required. Apply command filtering to reject unauthorised CEC commands.

title: HDMI HDCP Not Enforced
description: HDCP content protection is not enforced on the HDMI interface. Video/audio streams can be captured in cleartext.
remediation: Enable HDCP enforcement in device firmware.

title: HDMI DDC-CI Unauthorised Control
description: DDC-CI commands accepted over HDMI allow monitor control (brightness, OSD) without physical interaction with the display.
remediation: Disable DDC-CI in display firmware if remote monitor control is not required.

title: EDID Information Disclosure
description: EDID data was successfully read, disclosing monitor model, serial number, manufacturer, and capabilities.
remediation: No action required if EDID is functioning normally. Consider custom EDID for high-security deployments.

title: Unauthenticated Serial Console
description: A serial console (UART, RS-232) provided an interactive unauthenticated shell or bootloader prompt on connection.
remediation: Password-protect the serial console in firmware. Disable UART console in production builds.

title: Serial Console Baud Rate Identified
description: The serial port baud rate was auto-detected. The presence and configuration of a serial console is documented.
remediation: Review whether the console is accessible in production and restrict access if appropriate.

title: CAN Bus Frame Captured
description: CAN bus frames were captured from the device. Frame IDs and data payloads are documented for replay and fuzzing analysis.
remediation: Ensure CAN bus access is physically restricted. Document observed frame IDs against expected device behaviour.

title: CAN Bus Injected Frame Accepted
description: An injected CAN frame was accepted and processed by the device. CAN has no built-in authentication; any node on the bus can transmit arbitrary messages.
remediation: Implement a CAN firewall or gateway. Consider SecOC (ISO 21434) for safety-critical systems. Apply physical access controls to CAN connectors.

title: Zigbee Traffic Captured
description: Zigbee frames were captured from the device. Depending on the security profile, payloads may disclose network keys, sensor data, or command traffic.
remediation: Enable Zigbee AES-128 network and link layer encryption (Zigbee 3.0). Rotate network keys periodically.

title: Zigbee Flooding / Denial of Service
description: The Zigbee network showed signs of packet flooding tolerance (or lack thereof). Injection of excessive frames caused degraded responsiveness.
remediation: Implement rate-limiting on Zigbee join and message handling. Apply Zigbee channel scanning and jamming detection.

title: ARP / DHCP Traffic Reveals Network Configuration
description: Passive ARP or DHCP traffic captured during the ConfigDiscovery phase revealed network configuration details: default gateway, DNS servers, existing DHCP leases, and VLAN membership.
remediation: Informational — expected behaviour. Review whether observed network configuration aligns with intended design.

title: Plaintext Protocol in Boot Traffic
description: Traffic captured during device boot revealed cleartext protocols (Telnet, HTTP, FTP, TFTP) carrying potentially sensitive data including configuration pulls or update checks.
remediation: Replace plaintext boot-time protocols with TLS-protected equivalents. Use HTTPS for firmware update checks, SFTP for configuration retrieval.

title: Plaintext Protocol in Shutdown Traffic
description: Traffic captured during device shutdown contained plaintext protocol traffic, potentially including final state synchronisation or credential exchange.
remediation: Review and encrypt all shutdown-phase network communication.
